key_insight: Learning can organize synapses into dendritic clusters that help a neuron detect covariance structure, especially when dendritic nonlinearities and synaptic plasticity act together.
engineering_relevance: The result suggests that structured dendritic compartments and learned synaptic organization could improve neuromorphic or dendrite-aware models for classification tasks beyond standard linear-nonlinear networks.
method: Built Dendrinet, a neural architecture with hierarchical dendritic segments and sparse conductance-based synapses.
Trained the model on a Permuted-Covariance Classification task that is not solvable by a single-layer linear-nonlinear network.
Tested causal roles by turning off dendritic nonlinearities and shuffling learned excitatory/inhibitory synaptic organization.
evidence_signal: In simulation, the model solved the covariance classification task and formed excitatory and inhibitory functional synapse clusters when both dendritic nonlinearities and structural plasticity were enabled.
watch_item: The shuffling experiments alter more than cluster structure alone, so changes in performance cannot be attributed exclusively to FSCs.
paper_title: Synaptic clustering emerges from learning and supports covariance discrimination
